newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM talks economics, rights with China's Wu.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM talks economics, rights with China's Wu.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus discussed mutual economic interests with Chinese deputy premier Wu Bangguo, but differed on the subject of human rights during a meeting on Friday, Klaus's spokesman said.
"Both representatives exchanged opinions on the state and prospects of mutual relations in the political and economic spheres," a statement released after the meeting said.
The statement added that "another matter of discussion was problems of human rights".
"In this both parties stated varieties of opinion and the need for further intensive dialogue in this area," it said without elaborating.

Czech human rights groups, objecting to the Chinese Communist government's treatment of political dissidents, have protested against the low-key, five-day visit by Wu, one of China's six deputy premiers.
"They agreed on the bilateral interest in further economic cooperation for which exists good pre-conditions," the statement said.
Wu was also due to meet Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec on Friday and is scheduled to have meetings with other senior Czech ministers and politicians.
During the visit he will not, however, see President Vaclav Havel who left with his wife left for an 18-day private trip on Friday to the Italian Alps and the Netherlands.
Havel, once a dissident playwright imprisoned several times by a Communist government before its fall in 1989, has been a frequent diplomatic thorn in China's side.
The Czech president said last year that he regretted that Taiwan, which Bejing regards as a renegade province, is not a U.N. member.
However, the Czechs officially still recognise only China as a sovereign state and not Taiwan.
Havel angered China with a highly publicised meeting with Taiwanese Premier Lien Chan in 1995, forcing a hurried foreign ministry re-statement of the Czechs' official "One-China Policy".
